The note does not describe the underlying complex survey design or the specific sampling/replicate weight variables used in the database tables, so the exact weight variable name cannot be extracted from the provided text. data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024: Bahrain note summarizes teachers’ and principals’ self-reported perceptions and practices for lower secondary education, using OECD’s TALIS 2024 Database tables. The report focuses on statistically significant differences (and some changes) relative to the OECD average and highlights several domains: teachers’ background (age, gender, non-teaching experience), student diversity and special education needs, social and emotional learning support, technology use (including AI use), teachers’ learning opportunities (initial teacher education, induction/mentoring, continuous professional learning), teacher leadership/autonomy, professional relationships, status of the teaching profession, employment terms, demands/stress sources, and professional outcomes (lesson aims, well-being, satisfaction, and retention intentions). Because the note is descriptive and does not estimate predictive models, there are no ML performance metrics. Cross-country comparisons are explicitly cautioned as TALIS relies solely on self-reports and may be shaped by social and cultural context.
